content.title: About
content.content: Meat pizza that differs from classic pepperoni is made with a thick crust (over 1.5 cm) and topped with a variety of meats – beef, chicken, ham, bacon or sausage. Tomato sauce, mozzarella cheese and aromatic herbs complete the flavor profile.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: A thick crust retains the juiciness of the toppings and gives a more “bread‑like” bite.
Meat combos often use regional sausages, making each pizza unique in different areas.
Traditionally served in fast‑food restaurants, this pizza is also found in upscale pizzerias.
Combining several meats boosts protein content and makes the dish more filling.
Tomatoes are often roasted before being blended into the sauce, enhancing aroma.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: The meat provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue repair.

items.title: Iron content
items.content: Beef and chicken contain heme iron, which is more readily absorbed.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Mozzarella supplies calcium that supports bone health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and tomato sauce are good sources of B6 and B12 vitamins, important for the nervous system.

items.title: Energy density
items.content: Carbohydrates from the crust combined with protein from the meat provide sustained satiety.

items.title: High calorie count
items.content: Thick crust and meat toppings make the pizza calorie‑dense; moderation is advised.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Bacon and processed sausages can contain significant saturated fat, which should be considered in a heart‑healthy diet.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Meat products are often salty; people with hypertension should choose lower‑salt options.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger allergic reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pizza hot, sliced into wedges. Optional toppings include fresh vegetables, basil, or a drizzle of olive oil. For a lighter meal, eat a portion of pizza and complement it with a salad.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in an oven or grill to keep the crust crisp.
